chapters.html:
None dare to shake his hand in greeting.

 

For his hands burn as the blazing sun,

Soaked in the might of the flames.

While Mydei dressed like he cared little about really covering or protecting his body, his hands suggested otherwise, always sheathed with gilded gold. Seldom was he seen without his gauntlets – for he almost never took them off, not even in the baths, a place meant for stripping away all fineries and pretences.

It was in Okhema, the land dominated by souls that had never tasted the ruins of war, felt the sickly warmth of blood pouring over their bodies, where he developed this preference.

Now, Mydei wasn't insecure about his hands. He was simply weary of the widening eyes and flinching that followed whenever he shook his hands with someone, followed by them wrenching their hands away like they had been burnt.

Well, his hands did pack a lot of heat after all.

So, hands doused in the flames of the forge are eventually replaced by the cool steel of his gauntlets.

And they did nothing to soften Mydei’s profile – only emphasising the severity of his form, completing the image of the man shaped through conflict and death, not nurture. But no one really flinched at his touch anymore.

Phainon gradually weans him out of it.

Because naturally, if there had to be anyone who would decide to be a pain about it, it would be Phainon. He wouldn’t be the Deliverer he knew if he didn’t make it his mission to hunt something to nitpick and jibe about Mydei.

"Come on! Those fists of yours wouldn't pack such a punch if it weren't for those gauntlets." Phainon complains after one of their spars, massaging his cheek where a fresh bruise had started to form, “Don’t they give you an unfair advantage?"

"Unfair? You seriously believe that?”

“Oh-ho? Are you gonna start a whole lecture about how the-” Phainon clears his throat, adopting a mockingly deeper voice, “ruthlessness of true battle never cares about what the warrior wields?”

“You literally swing that hunk of metal at me, Deliverer while I fight you unarmed."

"You can say the gauntlets fare as your weapon, then."

“Then it is fair, by your logic – do you just like betraying your own points of debate if it’s of convenience to you?”

“It works on you like a charm, though.”

 

Phainon grins and Mydei scoffs at him.

 

“Believe whatever you'd like. Rather than a weapon – I'd say they protect you more – for my punches would hit a lot more had these gauntlets not weighed me down, Deliverer."

“Hah – no way they’re that heavy!”

 

Mydei responds by undoing one and tossing it towards the Heir. Phainon barely catches it in time and that smug look on his face is instantly replaced by shock as his body hunches over with the weight of it dragging him down.

 

"Wha-what the hell? They're this heavy?"

"Yes, you fool."

"You wear these the whole time!" Phainon straightens up, adjusting to the weight quickly enough, "Is that how you train that stamina of yours?"

"You could say so."

"I've never seen you without them. Not even in the baths."

"You think battles pause for a simple bath?"

Phainon frowns, "But it's still... overkill, is it not?"

 

Mydei hadn't given him a proper answer for that.

But that exchange had evidently bred a curiosity in Phainon, flourishing into a persistent, nosy interest. He was now quite intent on finding out why exactly Mydei never took them off – was it out of discipline? Passive stamina training? One of Mydei’s inexplicable eccentricities? 

After weeks of responding with little more than uninterested grunts, snappy profanities, and expertly timed absences whenever Phainon came too close, Mydei finally relents.

"What exactly is so fascinating about my hands to you, you HKS?"

"Until you tell me why you never take them off, I won't stop asking!"

"I have long given my answer to you."

"Too bad, I don't believe you!"

Mydei kicks out at him and Phainon neatly dodges him with a chuckle.

"Fine." Mydei hisses, taking off his gauntlets, "This is why I don't take them off."

Mydei holds out his hand to him and the gesture appears to catch Phainon mildly off-guard. He grants a few seconds to decode whatever his mysterious intentions were, before tentatively reaching out and grabbing his hand.

Of course Mydei sees it coming.

The way Phainon’s blue eyes widen.

The way his posture tenses as if he was barely suppressing a flinch.

Mydei doesn’t wait for him to wrench his hand away this time.

He pulls away himself.

"See? Satisfied with the answer, Deliverer-"

Phainon grabs his hand back.

Mydei doesn’t move – couldn’t move while Phainon stares down at their interlaced fingers with a quizzical look. He doesn’t grin; there is no mockery in his face, only contemplation. Then, Phainon releases him and stares at his own fingers, as if he expected them to look different. Before reaching out and pressing his hand against Mydei’s again.

Phainon’s fingers felt cool against his skin.

Everyone’s fingers felt cool against Mydei’s skin. But those touches never lasted – remaining brief and in passing, accidental or from acts of aggression not thought out well enough. They never lingered long enough for Mydei to ever remember what a cool touch was.

"...Are they supposed to be this warm?"

"It is much more than just 'warm' and you know it, Deliverer."

"Feels like I'm sticking my hand into a pot of boiling water." Phainon mutters.

Mydei stares down at their hands as well. There were callouses decorating the tips of Phainon's fingers – callouses carrying tales of relentless sword practices and poor attempts at embroidery. Deepened by battles that raged on for days without pause, bested by the warrior’s own determination to see them through to the end. By quiet, repeated acts of service – helping a weary local with goods too heavy to lift, hauling groceries for the elderly, hammering on the roofs that had cracked during Nikador's assault. Marks forged from constant strain, fuelled by a warm heart.

Mydei hadn’t realised how foreign the sensation was – had never got to hold hands long enough to properly feel such marks, to understand the stories they held. It felt bizarre, that just a touch alone could tell…so much.

And this was just from Phainon’s fingers alone. There were probably more of them, hidden beneath the gloves that hid the swordmaster's palms.

"Sane people who stick their hands in boiling water also remove them. I don't see you doing it."

Phainon looks up, eyes boring into his, no longer shocked or afraid.

"I don't really want to."

It becomes a quiet habit of sorts between them. Catching Phainon's stray gazes aimed at his covered hands, lingering too long for them to be any coincidence. Mydei ignores them at first but he expected it to be a battle he would lose; he knew Phainon’s persistency could wear down even the toughest of barriers.

In their moments of solitude, when the gazes of the world and the expectations of the rest were no longer upon them, Mydei would wordlessly take off his gauntlets and place them at the side. Stretch his fingers in the cooling air that hits them before curling them and then repeat. Phainon would watch this exercise with intrigue. Mydei doesn’t fully understand it, sometimes – why did this fool find even the smallest, the most mundane things about him so fascinating?

After staring for some time, Phainon would grab his bared hands, like a child handed a new toy. He would hold them like that, quiet and musing. Pressing, brushing, kneading at his flesh with his fingers. Curious. Exploring.

It doesn’t take long for Phainon to start taking his own gloves off as well for these moments. Letting Mydei feel up his hands in return. Giving back that very quiet trust that Mydei had offered.

Pressing, brushing, kneading at his flesh with his fingers. Curious. Exploring.

His palms had more callouses. More defined. Mydei wasn't surprised; Phainon was a swordsman after all, a seasoned one as well. Mydei's own hands were coarse like any warrior’s but his healing did not leave many marks behind for him to learn what callouses felt like.

On Phainon, they felt strange. Like anomalies. Yet so, so fitting.

Eventually, it doesn't just stop at gauntlets.

"Does your whole body run this hot?"

"Yes."

White locks dance over his eyes. Mydei had tugged off his upper robes as well, having them hang around his waist – not that they concealed much in the first place, scant as they were.

Phainon's fingers felt cool against his skin. Skimming over the dips of his bare shoulders, trailing towards the curves of his biceps. Following the muscles lining his stomach and flank, brushing his ribs, travelling down to the slop of his hip. Tracing the red painted across his chest and arms.

Pressing, brushing, kneading at his flesh with his fingers. Curious. Exploring.

“Isn’t it uncomfortable?”

"No." The extremes of agony were the first thing Mydei had gotten used to in the times of his earliest memories. The freezing waters of the Sea of Souls had not been kind – bitter and unrelenting towards the frail body of a child abandoned in their torrents, viciously demanding his endurance until numbness settled upon him like a makeshift haven. There were no shores for him to drift to, no blankets waiting there to swaddle him up with.

He had to be his own hearth to drift towards, his own flame to chase.

But Mydei hadn’t expected having to silence his longing for tenderness would make him completely untrained to receiving it. Because now, he was uncomfortable. Felt strange having his honed, toughened body be subjected to touches so cool and fleeting, so careful.

And Mydei's body knew what it was to feel the touch of another but those touches hadn't been kind in the slightest. He knew how sharp claws raked through his skin, the unforgiving cold of blades and arrowheads burrowing into his flesh, the throbbing pain of fists against his body.

And these touches were so tender, so careful, so brimming with life and curiosity, fingers cooled and slightly clammy with sweat – Phainon was straddling Mydei's thighs as he did it and the mere sight of it would have driven him mad had he not been so swept away by how strange his touches felt. The unfamiliarity of each caress, the delicacy driving each brush against his skin – it was all consuming him more.

So gentle, so new, so foreign.

Mydei's fingers dig into the sheets as Phainon touches his torso to his heart’s content. Aching to touch him as well. Let his own hands indulge too, after keeping them locked away in the steeled cage of his gauntlets, never allowing them to truly touch.

Of course Phainon notices his subtle agitation.

Peels away his own clothes.

Slowly tilts to the side, letting himself fall and sink into the mattress, letting Mydei flip over and cage him in. Willingly leaves himself open to him, lets him feel his own body this time.

Toned and sculpted just like Mydei’s.

Marred with numerous scars unlike Mydei’s.

Cool to touch and mortal unlike Mydei’s.

Phainon doesn't hide his tension from the heat that thrummed within Mydei's fingers. He does not conceal it, nor does he try and run from it. He embraces it, lays there prone and observant, watching the care with which Mydei touches him.

It felt strange. Touches, for Mydei, were something he wielded with weary care, avoiding it as much as he could, or burning with destructive ferocity, with the intent to vanquish, to beat into submission.

It felt strange, how he indulged with Phainon this time, a man who has already tasted the violence of his touch from their many battles, now seeing him so careful.

Mydei knew more than anyone else that Phainon was hardly anyone delicate and yet he couldn't help but keep his touches slow and trembling, looking up to see every reaction of his to every inch his fingertips grazed. Mydei also knew his touches couldn't be pleasant, couldn't be something anyone could get used to yet he touches Phainon with the assurance that he could take it.

And then, something else begins to grow between them – too fluid and subtle to be acknowledged as a ‘habit’, too frequent to mean nothing. Hands squeezing beneath tables. Fingers delving underneath shirts and robes and into gaps that gloves and gauntlets couldn't fully cover, circles traced against bare skin. Nails lightly scratching into palms, thumbs tracing the insides of their wrists. Little moments that developed in the hushes between them, in the moments where gazes looked elsewhere; their own and of those around them. Slow, unhurried, completely their own.

Mydei finds himself craving it, unconsciously so. At random moments, at times even when his mind was occupied with something else.

His fingers keep searching for that cool skin; his body craves being touched like it wasn't some indestructible pit of flames.

And Phainon indulges him. Every time. Like he was dutybound. With the vigour of a man who would willingly walk into flames for him.

Mydei would touch his jaw, trace his thumb along his lips, press his own lips against eyelids fluttered shut.

It must feel too much. The heat must be too much.

"Is it not?"

"It is not."

"My temperature isn't normal. It isn't supposed to feel normal, Deliverer."

"It doesn't. But your touch also feels too gentle for it to hurt like you think it does, Mydei."

Phainon cups his face between his palms. It is so foreign, so delicate and Mydei nuzzles into his hands anyway.

"Why are you so warm?" Phainon whispers.

"..."

"I often wonder if you have been running a shitty fever all this time."

"Perhaps. Maybe it's my curse, because my body refused to give in no matter how frigid the waters of death turned, fighting back and turning warmer and warmer until it was hot enough to boil those very waters demanding my demise."

"..."

"And yet you find my touch desirable? Refuse to flinch away from it?"

"Why would I not?" Phainon huddles closer. His lips felt cool against his throat, "If you stay warm enough for your body to never go cold, why would I ever want anything else?"

Mydei doesn't answer. His fingers aimlessly wander his body again. It still felt all too strange to get to touch someone like this. Yet so, so correct all the same.

Pressing, brushing, kneading at his flesh with his fingers. Curious. Exploring.

Phainon has felt the touch of many kinds of hands, varying in texture and temperature. Tribios’ feeling warm and plump to touch whenever he leaned down to give her a high-five, Anaxa’s feeling scratchy and dry from neglect whenever he got annoyed with him and grabbed his hand to make him rewrite whatever he had deemed nonsensical, Aglaea’s feeling hauntingly smooth whenever they brushed against his on occasion. He has never felt Castorice’s, for obvious reasons but he has heard her mention they were icy cold.

Mydei’s hands felt like holding onto lumps of heated coals.

"...Are they supposed to be this warm?"

"It is much more than just 'warm' and you know it, Deliverer."

It doesn’t burn the way Phainon expects it to, however – perhaps the temperature was similar to a flame’s, but it inflicts no damage on his skin to make him instinctively pull away.

Or perhaps Phainon was just strange; because Mydei had mentioned, in passing, about how everyone who touched him just flinched.

Maybe it was because it was Mydei. Because whatever they shared always came with bruises; physical discomfort was part and parcel of their bond – breathlessness from sudden races together, aches from their sparring matches and impromptu roughhousing, light-headedness from their endurance contests in the baths, sore hands from arm-wrestling matches, nausea from the portions of food Mydei purposefully cooked like shit for him.

So what if Mydei’s hands felt like they could char him to a crisp? There was no threat in that heat alone. Hell – this was the softest physical language they had ever spoken to each other with.

"My temperature isn't normal. It isn't supposed to feel normal, Deliverer."

"It doesn't. But your touch also feels too gentle for it to hurt like you think it does, Mydei."

But he still sees hesitation in Mydei’s gait whenever their hands touched, the brief, fervent glances to his face, observing Phainon’s reaction to the temperature. He feels up Phainon’s own hands with barely concealed wonder – a mix of indulgence and worry. It wasn’t difficult to silently understand that the man was getting to experience something that had always been out of reach for him.

From something tolerable, the burn becomes something…pleasant for Phainon. He enjoyed the heat, the sheer force of life thrumming beneath Mydei’s skin, running through his blood. He enjoyed the fact that it served no purpose save for Mydei’s own indulgence. It wasn’t necessity; it was just Mydei letting himself want.

“My body burns, yet it feels like you enjoy being seared by it, Deliverer.”

“Really?”

“Hmph, I still cannot say if it is you being insane or some buried masochism, that makes you seek something that feels like fire.”

“Isn’t it a basic instinct for living creatures?” Phainon returns, tracing his finger around Mydei’s belly button, “To seek warmth, to create a hearth for themselves, to bask in the heat that comes from huddling in their shelters? What are flames, if not to be chased?”

“…”

“Flames…chased – flame chase – did you get that-”

“Shut up.”

Phainon enjoys the comfort that slowly settles in with their touches going beyond just hands. Enjoyed pawing at Mydei’s body, feeling the heat with which his life blazed. And each time nails in how badly Phainon had wanted this, wanted to touch him without having to resort to the guises of battle and competition. Wanted to feel his hands on him for no reason but idle contact.

Mydei’s touches felt like he was starved, and Phainon mirrors it with acceptance. The unsaid intents remain so even when lips replace hands; Mydei’s mouth was as scorching as his palms, searing his affection onto Phainon’s flesh. He is oddly fascinated by Phainon’s body, particularly his scars, touching them with an almost reverent daze, kissing them like he was offering his worship.

Their intents remained as unsaid as the day they had started indulging in such a manner. But understood anyway.

Mydei does spend a generous bit of these moments studying his scars, tracing them as slowly as he could, as if he was trying to carve the shape and texture of them into his own brain. Phainon does find himself a little lost to this; Mydei did not have any of his own scars to offer.

Until Phainon decides it mattered not, making his move during one of their rare, peaceful evenings where they wiled away their hours wrapped in silence with idle touches, heedless combing of fingers through hair, abstract shapes traced over and over wherever their hands rested. Nuzzling into the heat of Mydei’s body, tracing his cool fingers over the bare skin of his nape.

“I do not have any scars for you to kiss, Deliverer.” Mydei had reminded him when Phainon pushed him down on the mattress, announcing his intent.

 

But Phainon remembered the wounds that should have left those, the traces of which incinerated by a body brimming with way too much life to contain. He had taken his time kissing each and every single one that he could remember, even if it meant briefly recalling all the painful moments he had seen his partner maimed.

And how Mydei had gazed upon him as he did, tense yet waiting, confused but observing – so used he was to pain being inflicted on his body, left unacknowledged with skin left so spotless after each wound. Phainon kissed the spots, imagined feeling skin slightly raised, left uncomfortably taut and discoloured.

“It matters – I don’t care if you could heal from a papercut in a second. Maybe you wouldn’t have stepped in if you could die – but you still hurt, you still bleed, you still feel pain and that is enough for me for it to matter.”

How content Mydei was to only expect pain. A mild rage had clouded his mind as Phainon littered his body with kisses, lips brushing against skin too smooth to have ever been scratched. No marks on it, save for the crimson inks lined throughout – just lingering echoes of pain Mydei probably felt only in memory. Phainon wondered how his lips felt on the spots where agony had once bloomed, to soon be forgotten.

How accepting Mydei was, to never expect a tender touch or quiet reverence, believing that the blood that boiled beneath his skin was reason enough for him to go a lifetime without knowing what a gentle hand felt like – to believe that was justified.

And then Mydei relents, offering to guide him the wounds he had suffered in the years long past, when Phainon hadn’t been there to see them. Small tales, with not too many details to follow – just enough for Phainon to understand that Mydei was letting it in; the tiny consolations long due. Allowing himself to drift towards those small specks of warmth.

And at least that, for Phainon, was enough, even if it was just embers in the present. They were flames to be chased, nonetheless.
